text: Git branching is an important part of a version control workflow. When you work on a new feature, you create a separate feature branch instead of changing the main code directly. This keeps your work safe and organized. After you finish, you merge your branch back into the main branch. Many teams use pull requests so that other developers can review the changes before merging. This process helps teams work together without confusion. If something goes wrong, you can easily return to an earlier version. Learning how to use branches well makes teamwork much smoother and helps keep your project clean and stable.
